newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 8.0 trln lire Btp, Cct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy seen issuing 8.0 trln lire Btp, Cct.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is expected on average to issue some 8.0 trillion lire worth of fixed-rate bonds (Btp) and floating-rate certificates (Cct) at its mid-month auction, a Reuter poll of analysts said.
The forecasts range from 6.0 to 9.5 trillion lire.
There is no paper expiring at this time.

The Treasury has announced that on October 15 it will offer a fifth tranche of September 1, 3003 Ccts with a first coupon of 4.55 percent, and a 15th tranche of July 1, 2006 Btps carrying an 8.75 percent coupon.
On October 16, the Treasury will auction a third tranche of both October 1, 1999 and September 15, 2001 Btps.

"It will be a fairly large auction seeing that at the beginning of the month only 13.5 trillion lire worth of paper was issued against 24.5 trillion lire worth expiring," said Paolo Cipollone of Credit Italiano.
Chiara Manenti of Caboto Sim noted that the Treasury needed to finance October borrowing needs which analysts estimate at 17 trillion lire.

Banca Commerciale Italiana (BCI) analysts said the Treasury would probably close the July 2006 Btp issue with the next auction. "The Treasury could keep it open but the coupon is now out of line with market values.

At its auction at the beginning of October, the Treasury issued new three-year Btps with a lower coupon of 7.50 percent against 8.25 percent and new five-year paper with a coupon of 7.75 percent against a previous 8.25 percent.
The Treasury will detail the amounts on offer on Thursday.
